audit.whatIsWrong: The whole difficulty read leans on 'his passive shield' and 'his passive absorbs your burst'. Galio has no passive shield. Not one of his five abilities is named anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Colossal Smash is an empowered basic attack that deals bonus magic damage in an area every few seconds — offence, not a shield. Telling a Rumble player to rush level 1 'before his passive shield activates' points at a timing that does not exist, and it hides the real early threat: a free empowered auto whenever he steps into range.
audit.corrected: Colossal Smash is an empowered auto every few seconds, not a shield. The level-1 window is real but it closes to Winds of War's 825 range at level 2, not to a passive coming online.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike says 'never Equalizer into a chokepoint unless Galio's R is confirmed on cooldown' with no cooldown number and no mention of the ability's targeting condition.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s — the longest cooldown in this lane by far — and it must be aimed at an ALLY's position, not a free point on the map. With no ally in range he cannot use it on you at all. Both facts turn a vague warning into a countable spike.
audit.corrected: Hero's Entrance is 180s at rank 1 and lands on an ally's position, so it does nothing to you alone in the side lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction of this lane is absent: Shield of Durand's taunt is 275 range and Galio moves slowly the whole time he is charging it, while Electro Harpoon is an 850-range slow he cannot outrun.
audit.why: A slowed Galio charging a 275-range taunt cannot close before the charge resolves. Harpooning him the moment the charge starts is a hard counter to the ability the page correctly identifies as his main trading tool, and it was never stated. Justice Punch (650 range, 11 to 7s) is then his only gap-closer.
audit.corrected: Harpoon him the instant Shield of Durand starts charging — he is already crawling, the taunt only reaches 275, and a double slow means it resolves on empty air.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block names only Justice Punch and gives no numbers.
audit.why: Justice Punch 11 to 7s, Shield of Durand 18 to 14s, Winds of War 11 to 7s, Hero's Entrance 180 to 140s. The two that decide the lane are Justice Punch and Shield of Durand.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block now carries Justice Punch's 11-to-7s and Shield of Durand's 18-to-14s.

edits.after: Level 1 is your only clean window — Galio has no MR items and only Colossal Smash, an empowered auto every few seconds, so there is no shield to race. Take Flamespitter first, stand at the tip of the 600 cone, and grind his HP. At Level 2 Winds of War pokes you from 825, outranging your cone entirely, and Shield of Durand sets up a taunt that drags you in on his terms. Respect the charge: he moves slowly the whole time he winds it up and the taunt only reaches 275, so harpoon him and walk sideways, never straight back.

The moment he hits Level 2 he can Q poke you back from outside your cone, and his W sets up a taunt that brings your Flamespitter damage into him on his terms, not yours. Respect the taunt angle: walk sideways when he winds W up, never straight back into him.

edits.after: Late game Galio's MR stack turns Equalizer from a fight-winner into a zoning inconvenience he walks through with Shield of Durand up. Your value is cross-map — find enemy clusters that do NOT include Galio, hit those with Equalizer, and let your team follow. notes: Biggest fix: the page repeatedly described a 'passive shield' for Galio. Colossal Smash is an empowered basic attack dealing bonus magic damage in an area — there is no passive shield in his kit. Second fix: Hero's Entrance targets an ALLY's position, so a lone side-lane Galio cannot use it against you; the page treated it as a free teleport onto your Equalizer. Two _missing-interactions entries for this pairing are misfires and were not written: 'knockup-enabler (Scrap Shield W vs Hero's Entrance R)' — Scrap Shield is a shield plus move-speed burst with no displacement, and rumble.json's 'knockup' and 'terrain' flags on W contradict Riot's own description; and 'autoreset (Colossal Smash P)' — Riot's text says the next basic attack deals bonus damage, which is not an attack reset. The page's claim that Shield of Durand grants damage reduction is not spelled out in Data Dragon (it says only 'charges a defensive stance'); I kept the existing wording rather than invent or delete, but it is unverified from the kit file.
